\section[humilde]{humilde — humble; poor}

\label{lesson:ES-C726-humilde}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to make up, then the Spanish for to pretend.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: humilde}
\textbf{humilde} — \textquotedblleft{}humble; poor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A pesar de su fama, es muy humilde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Despite her fame, she is very humble.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Una familia humilde} is a poor family.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{humilde} is inherited from Latin \emph{humilis} \textquotedblleft{}low, lowly\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{humus} \textquotedblleft{}earth, ground\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{humilde}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{humilde}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{humilde}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to make up, then the Spanish for to pretend, then say \emph{humilde} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does humilde mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Humble; poor\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la humildad]{la humildad — humility}

\label{lesson:ES-C726-humildad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to pretend, then the Spanish for humble.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la humildad}
\textbf{la humildad} — \textquotedblleft{}humility\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[modesto]{modesto — modest}

\label{lesson:ES-C726-modesto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for humility, then the Spanish for vanity.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: modesto}

\section[presumir]{presumir — to show off, to boast}

\label{lesson:ES-C726-presumir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for vanity, then the Spanish for modest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: presumir}
\textbf{presumir} — \textquotedblleft{}to show off, to boast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Le gusta presumir de su coche.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He likes to show off his car.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Presumir de algo}. Also to presume: \emph{se presume inocente}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{presumir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{praesūmere} \textquotedblleft{}to take beforehand\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{sūmere} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
